title: Coupon codes at checkout
one_liner: You asked for a coupon-code field at checkout so the Black Friday campaign can hand out 15%-off codes.
status_line: Almost done: the coupon field works and PR #142 passed review, but it needs your call on stacking and a Stripe key before it can merge.

last_checked.what: PR #142 state and CI checks on GitHub; staging checkout page loads with the coupon field

asked_last.quote: So can we ship this before Friday?
asked_last.answer: Yes, if you answer the stacking question and add the Stripe test key today; merge and deploy take about 30 minutes after that.

for_you.what: Should a coupon code stack with products that are already on sale?
for_you.why: Black Friday puts 40 products on sale. If codes stack, a 15% code on a 30%-off item gives 45% off, below cost on 6 of them. The code path for each answer is written; only the rule is missing.
for_you.recommend: Don't stack: apply the code only to full-price items. It protects margin on the 6 below-cost products and matches how the last campaign worked.

options.label: Don't stack (full-price items only)
options.reply: Coupons should not stack with sale prices: apply the code to full-price items only, show a note on sale items, then finish the PR.

options.label: Stack, capped at 40% total
options.reply: Let coupons stack with sale prices but cap the combined discount at 40%, then finish the PR.

options.label: Stack with no cap
options.reply: Let coupons stack with sale prices with no cap, then finish the PR.

for_you.then: I wire the chosen rule into the cart total, add two tests for it and push to PR #142; about 20 minutes.

for_you.what: Add the Stripe test secret key to the staging environment as STRIPE_SECRET_KEY.
for_you.why: Staging still uses an expired key, so the end-to-end checkout test fails at payment. Only you have access to the Stripe dashboard.
for_you.recommend: Create a restricted test key with only Coupons and PaymentIntents write access, so staging cannot touch live data.

options.label: Done, key added
options.reply: I added the new Stripe test key to staging as STRIPE_SECRET_KEY. Re-run the end-to-end checkout test.

for_you.then: I re-run the end-to-end checkout test on staging; about 5 minutes.

for_you.what: Maya (design) is checking the coupon field's mobile layout.
for_you.why: She asked to see it before it ships; the message went out Mon 26 Oct with a staging link.
for_you.then: If she asks for changes I apply them before merge; otherwise nothing.

origin.quote: Marketing wants to send 15% off codes for Black Friday. Add a coupon field to checkout that validates codes against Stripe and shows the discount before payment.

paragraphs.text: A coupon-code box on the checkout page of the Acme shop. Shoppers type a code, the shop checks it with Stripe (the payment provider), and the new total shows before they pay.
Marketing is emailing 15%-off codes for Black Friday on Fri 30 Oct. Until now the shop had no place to enter a code, so the campaign could not run.

The field, the Stripe check and the cart math were built on Fri 23 Oct and Sat 24 Oct. A review on Tue 27 Oct found that expired codes showed a blank error and that totals could round one cent wrong; both are fixed. Testing stopped at payment because staging's Stripe key has expired.
You added a limit of one code per order on Mon 26 Oct. Whether codes stack with sale prices never came up until the review, so that is still open.

more.text: The discount is applied per line item in cents and rounded down, so the total never shows a fraction of a cent. The cart recomputes on every quantity change, and the code is re-checked with Stripe right before payment in case it expired mid-session.

decisions.what: Validate codes live against Stripe instead of keeping our own coupon table.
Allow only one coupon code per order.
Round each line's discount down to the cent, so the shop never gives away more than the code promises.

done.outcome: Expired or unknown codes now show a clear message ("This code has expired") instead of a blank red box.
done.before: Any invalid code showed an empty error.

done.outcome: 31 unit tests cover the discount math, including the one-code limit and rounding.

caveats.text: Stripe codes created by marketing must have the same names as in the email, including case.
caveats.matters: The check is case-sensitive; a mismatch means every shopper sees 'unknown code' on launch day.
